app.title: pcbCAM
app.tagline: From Gerber to G-code, right in the browser
header.openHint: Import Gerber, Excellon or Gerber drill files from your computer. Nothing is sent over the internet.
header.exampleHint: Load the FTDI_Max board (bottom copper and drills) to discover the software.
empty.title: No board loaded
empty.body: Drop your Gerber and drill files here, or open them from your computer. Everything is computed in the browser: your files never leave your machine.
empty.formats: Supported formats: Gerber RS-274X and X2, Excellon, drill data as Gerber (Proteus), and a zip archive holding them.
drop.hint: Drop the files to import them
layers.title: Project
layers.color: Display colour of the layer (no effect on machining)
layers.up: Move the layer up: it is drawn over the next one
layers.down: Move the layer down: it is drawn under the previous one
layers.remove: Remove the layer from the project
view.measureHint: Click two points to measure. Escape to stop.
view.canvasLabel: Board view. Wheel to zoom, drag to move, arrow keys and +/− on the keyboard.
warning.unterminatedCommand: Unterminated command at the end of the file
warning.noQuadrantMode: Arc without quadrant mode: multi quadrant assumed
warning.invalidArc: Impossible arc, drawn as a straight line
warning.flashInRegion: Flash not allowed inside a region, ignored
warning.negativeImage: Negative image not supported: read as positive
warning.contentAfterEndOfFile: Content after the end of file ignored
warning.formatGuessed: Coordinate format guessed: check the hole positions
warning.noToolSelected: Hole before any tool selection, ignored
warning.nonCircularAperture: Non circular aperture in a drill file, ignored
about.title: About pcbCAM
about.body: PCB CAM software of 8 Fablab Drôme: from Gerber files to G-code, entirely in the browser.
about.reference: Algorithms inspired by FlatCAM Plus (MIT licence), rewritten in TypeScript.
about.privacy: No file is sent over the internet.
help.panelIntro: Every explanation of the buttons and parameters, grouped by topic. Hover or select an element of the interface to see its help in place.
help.viewFit.title: Show everything
help.viewFit.body: Centres the view and adjusts the zoom to show all visible layers in full.
help.viewFit.advice: Shortcuts: F key or double click in the view.
help.viewGrid.title: Grid
help.viewGrid.body: Shows a millimetre grid behind the board. The spacing follows the zoom (1, 2 or 5 times a power of 10); one line in five is stronger.
help.viewGrid.advice: Shortcut: G key. The current spacing is shown in the status bar.
help.viewOrigin.title: File origin
help.viewOrigin.body: Shows the zero of the Gerber file coordinates: pink line towards positive X, green line towards positive Y. This is not the machine origin yet, which is chosen at export.
help.viewMeasure.title: Measure a distance
help.viewMeasure.body: Click a first point, then a second one: the status bar shows the horizontal (Δx) and vertical (Δy) gaps and the distance in millimetres.
help.viewMeasure.advice: Zoom in before clicking for more precision. Escape or M to stop.
help.viewCursor.title: Cursor position
help.viewCursor.body: Coordinates of the board point under the mouse, in millimetres, in the Gerber file frame.
help.viewScale.title: Display scale
help.viewScale.body: Number of screen pixels for one millimetre of board. The larger it is, the more the view is zoomed in.
help.viewGridStep.title: Grid spacing
help.viewGridStep.body: Distance in millimetres between two thin grid lines, chosen automatically from the zoom.
help.fileOpen.title: Open files
help.fileOpen.body: Imports the Gerber (copper, outline…) and drill files (Excellon or Gerber) exported by your CAD software, or the production zip archive holding them. You can pick several at once, or drop them on the window.
help.fileOpen.advice: Everything is computed in the browser: your files never leave your computer.
help.fileExample.title: Example board
help.fileExample.body: Loads the fablab FTDI_Max board (bottom copper and drills) to try the software without your own files.
help.layerType.title: Layer type
help.layerType.body: Role of the file guessed at import: top or bottom copper, outline, drill… It comes from the X2 attributes of the file when present, otherwise from its name.
help.layerType.warning: An "Unknown" type means the file could not be recognised: check it is the layer you expect.
help.layerWarnings.title: Warnings
help.layerWarnings.body: Number of places of the file that caused trouble while reading (unknown command, guessed format…). The details, with line numbers, are under "Details".
help.layerWarnings.warning: A guessed coordinate format can shift or scale the board: check the holes against the copper.
help.language.title: Language
help.language.body: Switches every text of the interface and of the help between French and English. The choice is remembered by this browser.
help.theme.title: Theme
help.theme.body: Look of the interface: automatic (follows the computer setting), light or dark. The board view stays dark so the layers stand out.
help.about.title: About
help.about.body: Software version, licence and links to 8 Fablab Drôme.
help.diameter.title: Diameter
help.diameter.body: Width of the cutting part of the tool. For a V-bit, what matters is the actual width at the cutting depth, not the shank diameter.
help.diameter.advice: Measure it with a calliper or trust the maker's datasheet.
help.tipAngle.title: Tip angle (V-bit)
help.tipAngle.body: Angle of the tool cone. The smaller it is, the thinner the cut stays as the tool goes deeper.
help.tipAngle.warning: A wide angle quickly widens the cut if the board is not flat.
help.tipDiameter.title: Tip diameter (V-bit)
help.tipDiameter.body: Width of the flat at the end of the tool. It is the narrowest possible cut.
help.tipDiameter.warning: A broken tip makes the tool wider than advertised.
help.feedXY.title: XY feed rate
help.feedXY.body: Speed of the tool while cutting, in millimetres per minute.
help.feedXY.advice: 120 to 150 mm/min for isolation on a small hobby CNC.
help.feedXY.warning: Too fast: broken tool or burrs. Too slow: overheating.
help.feedZ.title: Z feed rate (plunge)
help.feedZ.body: Speed of the tool going down into the material, in millimetres per minute.
help.feedZ.advice: About a third of the XY feed rate.
help.spindleSpeed.title: Spindle speed
help.spindleSpeed.body: Rotation speed of the tool, in revolutions per minute.
help.cutDepth.title: Cutting depth
help.cutDepth.body: Distance below the copper surface reached by the tool. Copper is 35 µm thick: going through it is enough.
help.cutDepth.warning: Too deep = wider cut with a V-bit.
help.depthPerPass.title: Depth per pass
help.depthPerPass.body: Thickness removed at each pass. The total depth is reached in several passes.
help.depthPerPass.advice: 0.3 to 0.5 mm when cutting out FR4.
help.passes.title: Number of passes (isolation)
help.passes.body: Number of concentric outlines around the tracks. More passes = more space between tracks and the remaining copper.
help.overlap.title: Overlap
help.overlap.body: Share of the cutting width common to two neighbouring passes.
help.overlap.warning: At 0 %, a copper hair can remain between two passes.
help.millingDirection.title: Milling direction
help.millingDirection.body: Climb milling: the tool turns in the feed direction, better finish on a rigid machine. Conventional milling: more tolerant of mechanical backlash.
help.millingDirection.advice: Conventional is advised on hobby CNCs with backlash.
help.peck.title: Peck drilling
help.peck.body: Depth drilled at each plunge in peck mode. Between plunges the drill comes out of the hole to clear the chips, then feeds down again from 0.5 mm above the board.
help.peck.advice: 0.5 mm in general; less for drills under 0.6 mm.
help.tabs.title: Tabs
help.tabs.body: Small bridges of material left on the outline so the board does not come loose while machining. They are spread along the cut, each on a straight part, and kept only in the last passes.
help.tabs.advice: 2 to 4 tabs, 1 to 2 mm wide. Break them with pliers and sand them.
help.tabHeight.title: Tab height
help.tabHeight.body: Board thickness left under each tab, measured from the bottom of the board. Passes deeper than the top of the tabs rise over them.
help.tabHeight.advice: About 0.5 mm on a 1.6 mm board.
help.cutoutMargin.title: Cutout margin
help.cutoutMargin.body: Extra distance between the board edge and the cut, on top of the end mill radius. Without an outline layer, the cut goes around the copper at this distance.
help.cutoutMargin.advice: 0 when an Edge.Cuts outline exists, 1 to 2 mm otherwise.
help.nonIsolated.title: Non isolated area
help.nonIsolated.body: Place where the tool is too wide to pass between two copper features. A short circuit is likely.
help.nonIsolated.advice: Choose a thinner tool or reduce the depth (V-bit).
help.travelZ.title: Travel height (travel Z)
help.travelZ.body: Height at which the tool moves between two cuts.
help.travelZ.advice: 1 to 2 mm, above clamps and fixtures.
help.safeZ.title: Safe height (safe Z)
help.safeZ.body: Retract height at the start, at the end and at tool changes.
help.safeZ.advice: 10 to 20 mm, always above travel Z.
help.origin.title: Origin
help.origin.body: Point of the board matching the machine zero: set the machine on this point before running the file.
help.origin.advice: Lower left corner: the simplest to set on the machine.
help.mirror.title: Mirror
help.mirror.body: Flips the drawing left to right to mill the bottom side of a board turned over. The milling direction chosen is kept.
help.mirror.advice: Required for the back side of a double-sided board, turned over on the machine. Leave unticked if the layer is milled as it appears on screen.
help.postProcessor.title: Post-processor
help.postProcessor.body: Translates the toolpaths into the G-code dialect of the machine: move words, tool change, spindle, comments. Each machine has its own.
help.postProcessor.advice: Snapmaker Artisan for the Artisan; GRBL 1.1 for most small CNCs; Marlin for a 3D printer board; LinuxCNC for a PC driven machine.
sg.title: Brand styleguide
sg.intro: Internal validation page: colours, fonts, components, stickers, help and patterns as implemented. Switch the theme to compare light and dark.
sg.contrastNote: Measured contrast ratio of the text on its background (WCAG AA: 4.5 for body text).
sg.titles: Bebas Neue: titles, sections, stickers, key figures (always in capitals)
sg.homeTitle: Home title slanted by −10° (home screen only)
sg.body: Karla: everything else in the interface, 300 to 800, with italics
sg.helptipsNote: Hover, select with the keyboard or long press these parameters. Parametric illustrations come with the parameters themselves (milestone J5 onwards).
sg.patternsNote: Two-colour patterns, only on the home screen, empty states and About, never behind dense text.
sg.calloutSuccess: The tool fits between all tracks.
sg.calloutWarning: Less than 10 % margin between the tool and the minimum clearance.
sg.calloutError: 3 areas cannot be isolated with this tool.
sg.calloutInfo: The coordinate format was read from the file.
sg.calloutHelp: Start with the board analysis to choose your tools.
illus.toolProfile: Tool profile ({type}): diameter {diameter} mm, tip {tip} mm, angle {angle}°
illus.vbitSection: {angle}° V-bit {depth} deep in the copper: cutting width {width}
illus.copperThickened: Copper thickness exaggerated to stay visible
illus.depthPasses: {count} passes of {perPass} mm to reach {depth} mm
illus.zHeights: Tool heights: safe {safe} mm, travel {travel} mm, cutting {depth} mm below the surface
help.boardThickness.title: Board thickness
help.boardThickness.body: Total thickness of the board, FR4 and copper included. It sets the depth of drilling and cutout, hence the number of passes.
help.boardThickness.advice: 1.6 mm for most boards; measure it with a calliper when in doubt.
help.boardThickness.warning: Too low: the board stays attached. Too high: the mill digs into the spoil board for nothing.
tabs.label: Panels
tools.title: Tool library
tools.resetConfirm: Replace the whole library with the original tools? Your tools will be lost (export them first if needed).
tools.toValidateNote: Starting values for a small CNC on FR4: to be validated on your machine.
tools.limitVbit: The deeper it goes, the wider the cut: {width} mm at {depth} mm.
tools.limitThin: Fragile tool: moderate feed and small depth per pass.
tools.limitDrill: Only drills round holes of its diameter; mill larger holes.
tools.limitCutout: {passes} passes to go through a {thickness} mm board.
tools.notPersistent: The browser refuses to store data: your changes will be lost when closing. Export the library to keep it.
tools.importError.notJson: This file is not a JSON file.
tools.importError.wrongFormat: This file is not an pcbCAM tool library.
tools.importError.newerVersion: This library comes from a newer version of pcbCAM.
tools.importError.invalidTool: No valid tool in this file.
editor.name: Name
issue.tipLargerThanDiameter: The tip must be between 0 and the tool diameter.
issue.tipAngleOutOfRange: The tip angle must be between 0 and 180°.
issue.depthNotPositive: The cutting depth must be above 0.
issue.depthPerPassNotPositive: The depth per pass must be above 0.
issue.depthPerPassAboveDepth: The depth per pass cannot exceed the total depth.
issue.spindleNotPositive: The spindle speed must be above 0.
issue.safeBelowTravel: The safe height must be at least the travel height.
issue.travelNotPositive: The travel height must be above 0.
analysis.title: Board analysis
analysis.empty: Import at least one copper layer to analyse the board.
analysis.isolationNote: From the most robust to the finest. Minimum clearance: {clearance} mm.
analysis.drillingNote: Nearest drill for each hole size.
analysis.grouping: Holes of {holes} mm are drilled with the same drill: {saved} fewer tool change(s).
analysis.noCutoutTool: No cutout mill in the library.
help.tabProject.title: Project tab
help.tabProject.body: List of the imported files and their layers: visibility, colour, order and reading details.
help.tabTools.title: Tools tab
help.tabTools.body: Your library of end mills, V-bits and drills, with their illustrated cards. It is stored in this browser.
help.tabAnalysis.title: Analysis tab
help.tabAnalysis.body: Board measurements (minimum clearance, thinnest track, holes) and advised tools for isolation, drilling and cutout.
help.toolAdd.title: New tool
help.toolAdd.body: Creates a tool of the chosen type, filled with common values, then opens its card to adjust it.
help.toolReset.title: Back to the original tools
help.toolReset.body: Replaces the library with the tools shipped with pcbCAM. Your tools are lost: export them first if needed.
help.toolBuiltIn.title: Tool to validate
help.toolBuiltIn.body: Tool shipped with pcbCAM: its values are a starting point for a small CNC on FR4, not a guarantee for your machine.
help.toolBuiltIn.advice: Try it on a board offcut, then save your settings: the tool becomes your own.
help.toolWidth.title: Cutting width
help.toolWidth.body: Width of the groove cut by the tool at its cutting depth. For a V-bit it depends on the tip, the angle and the depth; this width must fit between the tracks.
help.toolType.title: Tool type
help.toolType.body: Straight end mill (cuts across its whole width), V-bit (conical tip for fine isolation) or drill (drilling only).
help.toolType.advice: V-bit for isolation, end mill for cutout and large holes, drill for round holes.
help.toolUsage.title: Uses
help.toolUsage.body: Operations for which the tool is offered in the recommendations: isolation, drilling, hole milling or cutout.
help.minClearance.title: Minimum clearance
help.minClearance.body: Smallest distance between two distinct copper features (tracks, pads). The isolation tool must be narrower to fit everywhere.
help.minClearance.advice: Choose a tool whose cutting width leaves at least a 10 % margin.
help.minTrackWidth.title: Thinnest track
help.minTrackWidth.body: Width of the narrowest track of the file. A very thin track copes badly with a deflecting tool or too deep an isolation.
help.minTrackWidth.warning: Below 0.2 mm, milling the board becomes delicate.
help.holeSizes.title: Holes
help.holeSizes.body: Diameters of the holes found in the drill files, from the smallest to the largest, with their count.
help.zoomToSpot.title: Zoom to the area
help.zoomToSpot.body: Centres the board view on the tightest spot and highlights it.
help.isolationAdvice.title: Advised isolation tools
help.isolationAdvice.body: Each tool is compared with the minimum clearance: "Suitable" when it fits everywhere with a margin, "Borderline" with less than 10 % margin, "Too wide" when it cannot pass in some places.
help.isolationAdvice.warning: With a "Too wide" tool, neighbouring tracks may stay connected: a short circuit is likely.
help.drillingAdvice.title: Advised drills
help.drillingAdvice.body: For each hole size, the nearest drill of the library, with the gap in millimetres and percent. Holes too large for your drills are milled.
help.drillingAdvice.advice: A positive gap gives a slightly larger hole, often better for component leads.
help.drillGrouping.title: Drill grouping
help.drillGrouping.body: Close hole sizes can be drilled with the same drill: fewer tool changes, hence fewer setting risks.
help.cutoutAdvice.title: Advised cutout mill
help.cutoutAdvice.body: Mill offered to cut the board out, with the number of passes needed for the thickness and its depth per pass.
help.cutoutAdvice.advice: A 1.5 to 2 mm corn cob mill at 0.4 mm per pass suits FR4.
illus.isolationPasses: {passes} isolation pass(es) of {width} mm with {overlap} % overlap, seen from above
illus.climb: Climb milling: the tool turns with the feed, the copper kept is on the left of the path
illus.conventional: Conventional milling: the tool turns against the feed, the copper kept is on the right of the path
illus.nonIsolated: {width} mm tool wider than the {gap} mm gap: both pads stay connected
illus.isolated: {width} mm tool in a {gap} mm gap: the pads are separated
machining.empty: Import a copper layer to prepare the isolation.
machining.noTool: No isolation tool in the library: add a V-bit or a fine end mill.
machining.stale: Parameters changed: compute again to update the toolpaths.
machining.missingLayer: The layer of this operation was removed from the project.
machining.missingTool: The tool of this operation is no longer in the library.
machining.compareNote: Choose 2 or 3 tools: each one is computed with the parameters of the last isolation (or the default ones).
machining.previewLabel: Isolation preview with {tool}: toolpaths in green, non isolated areas in yellow
machining.timeNote: Estimated time without machine accelerations, rapids at {rapid} mm/min.
help.tabMachining.title: Machining tab
help.tabMachining.body: The three machining operations of the board, one step at a time: track isolation, drilling and cutout, with the toolpaths computed, the estimated time and the tool comparator.
help.isolationNew.title: New isolation
help.isolationNew.body: Creates an isolation operation on the first copper layer with the best rated tool for this board, then computes its toolpaths.
help.isolationLayer.title: Layer to isolate
help.isolationLayer.body: Copper layer whose tracks and pads the tool goes around to separate them from the rest of the copper.
help.isolationTool.title: Isolation tool
help.isolationTool.body: End mill or V-bit cutting the grooves around the copper. Tools are listed from the most to the least suitable for this board.
help.isolationTool.warning: A "Too wide" tool leaves neighbouring tracks connected.
help.combinePasses.title: Combined passes
help.combinePasses.body: Checked: all the passes of one group of tracks are cut in a row, which reduces travel. Unchecked: the first pass over the whole board, then the second, and so on.
help.combinePasses.advice: Usually checked; uncheck it to inspect the first pass before running the next ones.
help.isolationRun.title: Compute the isolation
help.isolationRun.body: Computes the tool paths in the background, then shows them on the board with the non isolated areas and the estimated time.
help.cutLength.title: Cutting length
help.cutLength.body: Total length of the grooves at one depth, and length of the empty moves between grooves. Several depth passes multiply the cut.
help.estimatedTime.title: Estimated time
help.estimatedTime.body: Machining time computed with the tool feed rates, every depth pass, the plunges and the rapid moves.
help.estimatedTime.warning: Estimate without accelerations: the machine will be a bit slower, mostly on small details.
help.zoneList.title: Non isolated areas
help.zoneList.body: Places where the tool is too wide to pass between two copper features, with their gap. Click an area to see it on the board.
help.compareTools.title: Tool comparator
help.compareTools.body: Computes the isolation of the same layer with 2 or 3 tools and shows them side by side: cutting width, estimated time, non isolated areas and a board preview.
help.compareRun.title: Run the comparison
help.compareRun.body: Computes the isolation with every chosen tool in parallel.
help.compareUse.title: Use this tool
help.compareUse.body: Creates an isolation operation with this tool, reusing the computation already made by the comparator.
help.isolationAdvanced.title: Advanced settings
help.isolationAdvanced.body: Settings rarely needed, folded away to keep the card simple.
help.extraOffset.title: Extra offset
help.extraOffset.body: Moves every pass this far away from the copper (FlatCAM "custom offset"). Tracks and pads keep a wider copper border.
help.extraOffset.advice: 0 in general. 0.02 to 0.05 mm to make up for a tool cutting wider than expected.
help.extraOffset.warning: Reduces the room the tool has to pass: check the non isolated areas after computing.
machining.drillingEmpty: Import a drill file (Excellon or Gerber X2) to prepare the drilling.
machining.noHoles: No hole in the files ticked.
machining.distanceDetail: {optimized} m instead of {file} m in the order of the file (nearest neighbour alone: {nearest} m)
machining.showFileOrder: Show the order of the file
machining.safety: {count} unsafe move(s) found: do not machine and report the problem.
machining.issue.noTool: Ø {diameter} mm: no tool chosen, {count} hole(s) not machined.
machining.issue.toolTooLarge: Ø {diameter} mm: the end mill is wider than the hole, {count} hole(s) not machined.
machining.issue.slotWithDrill: Ø {diameter} mm: {count} slot(s) milled with a drill, which cuts poorly sideways. Prefer an end mill.
machining.issue.drillTooSmall: Ø {diameter} mm: the drill is much smaller than the hole ({count} hole(s)).
illus.drillSimple: Simple drilling: one plunge down to {depth} mm
illus.drillPeck: Peck drilling: {count} plunges of {peck} mm down to {depth} mm
illus.drillDepth: {depth} mm hole in a {thickness} mm board
illus.holeMilling: {hole} mm hole milled with a {tool} mm tool, seen from above
illus.holeMillingBlocked: The {tool} mm tool is wider than the {hole} mm hole
illus.holeTooSmall: Tool wider than the hole: impossible
illus.holeMillingCaption: The tool centre turns {radius} mm from the centre
help.drillingNew.title: New drilling
help.drillingNew.body: Creates a drilling operation with every drill file of the project and, for each hole size, the tool recommended by the analysis, then computes it.
help.drillingLayers.title: Drill files
help.drillingLayers.body: Files whose holes are drilled together. Holes of the same diameter are grouped.
help.drillingLayers.advice: Make one operation for plated holes and another for non plated ones if you drill them at different times.
help.holeTool.title: Tool for a hole size
help.holeTool.body: Drill or end mill used for this diameter. With a drill, the difference between drill and hole is shown. With an end mill, the hole is milled along a helix.
help.holeTool.advice: Keep the drill proposed, or group close sizes on the same drill to avoid a tool change.
help.holeTool.warning: "Out of tolerance": the hole will be clearly larger or smaller than intended.
help.holeMilling.title: Milled hole
help.holeMilling.body: Hole too large for the drills: the end mill goes down along a helix on a circle, one turn per depth pass, then a last turn at the bottom.
help.holeMilling.advice: 1.5 mm corn cob mill for 3 mm mounting holes.
help.holeMilling.warning: The end mill must be smaller than the hole.
help.drillCycle.title: Drilling cycle
help.drillCycle.body: Simple: the drill goes down to the bottom in one go. Peck: it goes down by steps and comes out of the hole between steps to clear the chips.
help.drillCycle.advice: Simple on 1.6 mm FR4; peck for thick boards or very small drills.
help.drillDepth.title: Hole depth
help.drillDepth.body: Depth reached by every hole below the copper surface: the board thickness plus a margin into the spoil board.
help.drillDepth.advice: Board thickness + 0.2 mm (1.8 mm for 1.6 mm).
help.drillDepth.warning: Too short, the hole does not go through; far too deep, the drill reaches the table.
help.dwell.title: Dwell at the bottom
help.dwell.body: Pause of the drill at the bottom of every hole before going up, to finish the cut.
help.dwell.advice: 0 in general; 0.2 to 0.5 s if holes do not come out clean.
help.drillingRun.title: Compute the drilling
help.drillingRun.body: Groups the holes by tool, optimises the order of each tool (nearest neighbour then 2-opt) and estimates the duration.
help.drillDistance.title: Distance saved
help.drillDistance.body: Length of the moves between holes compared with the order of the file. The order is optimised tool by tool: nearest neighbour, then 2-opt, which removes crossings.
help.drillDistance.advice: Tick "Show the order of the file" to see the original route in grey dashes.
help.showFileOrder.title: Show the order of the file
help.showFileOrder.body: Draws in grey dashes the route between holes in the order of the file, to compare it with the optimised route (pink).
machining.cutoutEmpty: Import the board (copper or outline) to prepare the cutout.
machining.cutoutNoTool: No end mill of at least 0.8 mm in the library: add a cutout end mill.
machining.cutoutNoOutline: No outline layer: the cut goes around the copper and holes, at the margin chosen.
machining.tabsHint: Click the cut to add a tab, click a tab to remove it.
machining.cutoutIssue.tabsOverlap: Some tabs overlap: move them apart or make them narrower.
machining.cutoutIssue.tabTooHigh: The tabs are as high as the board: they would not be cut at all.
machining.cutoutIssue.noTabs: No tab: the board comes loose in the last pass and can be thrown by the end mill.
machining.cutoutIssue.tabsTooMany: Too many tabs for the length of the outline.
illus.cutoutTabs: {count} tab(s) {width} mm wide and {height} mm high, cut {margin} mm from the board
illus.tabsCaption: Width {width} mm, {height} mm of board kept out of {thickness} mm
help.tabWidth.title: Tab width
help.tabWidth.body: Length of board edge left attached at each tab. The tool stops before it, at its radius.
help.tabWidth.advice: 1 to 2 mm: enough to hold the board, easy to break.
help.tabHeight.warning: Equal to the board thickness, the tab would not be cut at all.
help.cutoutNew.title: New cutout
help.cutoutNew.body: Creates a cutout operation around the outline layer (or the copper when there is none), with the recommended end mill and 4 tabs.
help.cutoutSource.title: Board edge
help.cutoutSource.body: Outline layer giving the shape of the board (Edge.Cuts, GKO...). An outline drawn as a line is followed along the middle of the line.
help.cutoutSource.advice: Without an outline, the cut goes around the copper and holes with the margin chosen.
help.cutoutMode.title: Cut shape
help.cutoutMode.body: Exact shape: the end mill follows the board outline. Bounding rectangle: it goes around the smallest rectangle holding the board.
help.cutoutMode.advice: Rectangle for a rectangular board or a quick prototype.
help.cutoutTool.title: Cutout end mill
help.cutoutTool.body: End mill going through the board. Mills meant for cutout come first, then those needing the fewest passes.
help.cutoutDepth.title: Cutout depth
help.cutoutDepth.body: Depth of the cut below the surface: the board thickness plus a small margin into the spoil board. It is reached in several passes according to the depth per pass of the end mill.
help.tabsAuto.title: Spread the tabs
help.tabsAuto.body: Places the chosen number of tabs evenly along the cut again, the first in the middle of the longest straight side: in the middle of every side for 4 tabs on a rectangle.
help.tabsEdit.title: Place the tabs on the board
help.tabsEdit.body: Turns on placing with the mouse: a click on the cut adds a tab, a click on a tab removes it. Dragging still moves the view.
help.tabMachine.title: Machine tab
help.tabMachine.body: Last steps, one at a time: the machine (travel, speeds), its post-processor with a live preview, then writing the G-code of the board and its simulation.
machine.title: Machine

help.machineTravel.title: Machine travel
help.machineTravel.body: Distance each axis can move. Work larger than the X or Y travel, or deeper than the Z travel, is reported before sending.
help.machineTravel.advice: Measure the travel really usable, vice, clamps and spoil board included.
help.maxSpindleSpeed.title: Maximum spindle speed
help.maxSpindleSpeed.body: Highest rotation speed of the spindle. A tool set above it is reported: the spindle would cap without warning.
help.maxSpindleSpeed.advice: The one given by the spindle maker; 18,000 rpm for the 200 W module of the Snapmaker Artisan.
help.maxFeed.title: Maximum feed
help.maxFeed.body: Highest cutting speed the axis accepts (XY or Z). A tool set above it is reported.
help.maxFeed.advice: Read GRBL settings $110 to $112 to know the speeds of your machine.
help.rapidFeed.title: Rapid move speed
help.rapidFeed.body: Speed of moves outside the material. It is used to estimate durations, and Marlin writes it on every G0.
help.rapidFeed.advice: Start cautiously (1,000 to 3,000 mm/min) and raise it once you know the machine.
help.postCopy.title: Copy the profile
help.postCopy.body: Creates an editable copy of the profile, chosen for the machine used. Built-in profiles cannot be changed.
help.postUnits.title: G-code units
help.postUnits.body: Millimetres (G21) or inches (G20). Coordinates and feeds are converted; remember to put G20 in the program start for inches.
help.postUnits.advice: Millimetres, unless the machine is set to inches.
help.postComments.title: Comment style
help.postComments.body: In parentheses (GRBL, LinuxCNC), after a semicolon (Marlin) or no comment at all. Comments are written without accents.
help.postDecimals.title: Decimals
help.postDecimals.body: Number of digits after the decimal point of coordinates and feeds. 4 decimals in mm give 0.1 µm, far beyond the precision of the machine.
help.postArcs.title: Arcs
help.postArcs.body: G2 / G3: the machine draws arcs itself. Short segments: each arc is written as straight segments within 5 µm of the arc, for controllers without G2 / G3.
help.postFeeds.title: Feed writing
help.postFeeds.body: Only when it changes (F is modal for GRBL and LinuxCNC) or on every cutting line, as Marlin expects.
help.postRapidFeed.title: Rapid feed
help.postRapidFeed.body: Writes the rapid speed on every G0. Marlin needs it: without F it would make rapids at the feed of the last cut.
help.postLineNumbers.title: Line numbers
help.postLineNumbers.body: Adds N10, N20... at the start of G-code lines. Some older controllers ask for them; they make the file longer.
help.postCommands.title: Move words
help.postCommands.body: Words written for a rapid, a straight cut and the arcs: G00 or G0, G01 or G1... Each is a letter followed by a number.
help.postHeader.title: Program start
help.postHeader.body: Lines written after the header comments: units, absolute mode, XY plane, work offset. One command per line.
help.postHeader.advice: G21, G90, G17, G94 and G54 suit most machines.
help.postToolChange.title: Tool change
help.postToolChange.body: Sequence of a tool change: spindle stop, rise to {safeZ}, then M6 for a tool changer or an M0 pause for a change by hand. {message} names the tool to mount.
help.postToolChange.warning: GRBL refuses M6: keep an M0 pause.
help.postSpindle.title: Spindle
help.postSpindle.body: Lines starting and stopping the spindle. {spindleSpeed} is the speed of the tool. A short pause after starting lets the spindle reach its speed.
help.postDwell.title: Dwell
help.postDwell.body: Pause at the bottom of a hole. {seconds} or {milliseconds} depending on the controller: GRBL and LinuxCNC count seconds (G4 P), Marlin milliseconds (G4 P) or seconds (G4 S).
help.postFooter.title: Program end
help.postFooter.body: Lines written at the very end, after rising to the safe height and stopping the spindle, for example M2 (end of program).
help.postForbidden.title: Refused words
help.postForbidden.body: Words the controller does not know, separated by commas. When they appear in the written G-code, the line is reported.
help.postPreview.title: G-code preview
help.postPreview.body: G-code written by the profile for a small sample board, updated at every change. It is read back and checked (rapids, safe heights, machine limits) as your files will be.
post.description.grbl-1.1: Most small hobby CNCs. GRBL refuses M6: the tool change stops the spindle, rises to the safe height and pauses (M0) so the tool can be changed by hand.
post.description.marlin: Marlin firmware driving a spindle (3D printer board turned into a CNC). Comments with ';', feed on every move, M400 waits for the moves to end before stopping the spindle; M0 pauses with a message for the tool change.
post.description.linuxcnc: LinuxCNC (and Mach3 compatible controllers). T M6 changes the tool: LinuxCNC shows its own tool change dialog and waits.

help.mirror.warning: Isolation and drilling must share the setting, or the holes miss the pads.
help.exportOperations.title: Operations to write
help.exportOperations.body: Computed operations, in machining order: isolation, drilling (one tool after the other), cutout. Untick those not to send.
help.exportSplit.title: One file per operation
help.exportSplit.body: Writes one file per tool instead of a single one: useful to run each tool on its own, or when the machine dislikes tool change pauses.
help.exportRun.title: Write the G-code
help.exportRun.body: Writes the G-code of the chosen operations with the post-processor of the machine, checks it (safety rules, machine travel) and prepares the simulation.
help.exportText.title: G-code text
help.exportText.body: The G-code as it will be sent, in colours: moves in red, machine commands in purple, feeds in green, comments in grey.
help.exportEdit.title: Edit the G-code
help.exportEdit.body: Fixes the text by hand before downloading it. Safety rules are checked again on the edited text; the simulation shows the G-code written by pcbCAM.
help.exportEdit.warning: A mistake in the G-code can break the tool or the board: read it again before sending.
help.backplot.title: Simulation
help.backplot.body: Tool path read back from the written G-code and drawn on the board: cuts in green, rapid moves in pink, machine zero marked by a red cross, tool in yellow.
help.projectSave.title: Save the project
help.projectSave.body: Saves to a .pcbcam.json file the imported files, the layer display, the thickness, the tools, the machine, the operations and the export settings.
help.projectSave.advice: The file holds everything: it opens on another computer without the original files.
help.projectOpen.title: Open a project
help.projectOpen.body: Replaces the current project with the one of a .pcbcam.json file: files are imported again and operations computed again. The file can also be dropped on the window.
help.postLineNumbers.advice: Off in general; when the machine asks for it, start at 10 with a step of 10.
guide.title: My first board
guide.intro: From your Gerber files to the board cut out, step by step. Without files at hand, the FTDI_Max example board serves as a model.
guide.import.title: Import the files
guide.import.body: Open or drop the Gerber files of the board (copper, outline) and its drill files. Each file becomes a layer; its type is recognised on its own.
guide.analysis.title: Read the analysis
guide.analysis.body: pcbCAM measures the tightest gap between two copper features, the thinnest track and the hole sizes. The isolation tool must fit in the tightest gap.
guide.tools.title: Check the tools
guide.tools.body: The library holds starting values for a small CNC. Compare them with your real tools (tip and angle of the V-bits, drill diameters) before the first machining.
guide.isolation.title: Isolate the tracks
guide.isolation.body: The recommended tool goes around each track to separate it from the rest of the copper. Areas in yellow are places it cannot pass: change the tool if there are any.
guide.drilling.title: Drill
guide.drilling.body: Each hole size gets the nearest drill; holes too large are milled. The order of the holes is optimised to shorten the moves.
guide.drilling.none: No drill file in the project: step skipped.
guide.cutout.title: Cut out
guide.cutout.body: The cutout end mill goes around the board in several passes and leaves tabs so it stays in place to the end.
guide.export.title: Write the G-code
guide.export.body: Choose the origin (lower left corner recommended), write the G-code, watch the simulation, then download the file for the machine.
guide.machine.title: On the machine
guide.machine.body: Clamp the board flat, set the X / Y zero on the lower left corner and the Z zero on the copper with the isolation tool. Run the file: at each pause, change the tool, set the Z zero again, then resume.
help.guideOpen.title: "My first board" guide
help.guideOpen.body: Opens the step by step guide leading from importing the files to the machined board, showing the steps already done.
help.guideStep.title: Guide step
help.guideStep.body: Does the step for you with the recommended settings (or opens the place where it is done). Everything can be changed afterwards.
help.glossary.title: Illustrated glossary
help.glossary.body: Every help topic of the application, grouped by theme, with its illustrations, recommended values and warnings.
help.helpSearch.title: Search the help
help.helpSearch.body: Filters the glossary on a word of the title or the text, ignoring accents and capitals.
machine.presetAdded: Machine "{name}" added and chosen: check its values.
machine.issue.minAboveMax: The minimum spindle speed must be positive and below the maximum.
post.issue.invalidExtension: The extension has 1 to 5 letters or digits, without dot.
post.job.spindleBelowMachine: A spindle speed is below the machine minimum: the machine will raise it.
post.description.snapmaker-artisan: Snapmaker Artisan with the 200 W CNC module. The header lets the screen recognise a CNC file and show its time and size. The spindle takes its speed in rpm (M3 S, 8,000 to 18,000). No M6: a tool change stops the spindle, rises and pauses the job with M600; it resumes from the screen. Arcs are written as short segments, like the official Snapmaker post-processors.
help.machinePreset.title: Add a machine model
help.machinePreset.body: Adds a preset machine (GRBL milling machine, Snapmaker Artisan) with its travel, speeds and post-processor, and chooses it.
help.machinePreset.advice: Then check the Z travel really usable with your spoil board.
help.minSpindleSpeed.title: Minimum spindle speed
help.minSpindleSpeed.body: Lowest speed the spindle can hold. A tool set below it is reported: the machine would turn faster than planned.
help.minSpindleSpeed.advice: 0 when the spindle has no minimum; 8,000 rpm for the Snapmaker 200 W CNC module.
help.postFileHeader.title: File header
help.postFileHeader.body: Lines written at the very top of the file, as they are, for the screen or software of the machine. They may give values of the job: {lineCount}, {estimatedSeconds}, {xMin} to {zMax}, {workSpeed}, {spindlePercent}.
help.postFileHeader.advice: Empty for GRBL, Marlin and LinuxCNC; the ";Header Start" block for a Snapmaker.
help.postFileExtension.title: File extension
help.postFileExtension.body: Ending of the G-code files written, without the dot. Some machines only list their own extension.
help.postFileExtension.advice: nc in general; cnc for a Snapmaker.
machine.toolChangeFiles: One file per tool, Z zero set again
post.firstToolChange: First tool change (empty: same as the others)
export.separateFiles: {machine}: one file per tool. Before each file, mount the tool named and set the Z zero again on the board; the X / Y zero stays the one of the first file.
export.stepFirst: Mount the first tool, set the X, Y and Z origin, then run {file}.
export.stepNext: Mount the next tool, set the Z zero only, then run {file}.
help.machineToolChange.title: Tool change
help.machineToolChange.body: Pause: one file stopping at each tool change. One file per tool: the Z zero is set again with each tool before running its file, since tools do not have the same length.
help.machineToolChange.advice: One file per tool for the Snapmaker Artisan, which cannot set the zero during a pause.
help.machineToolChange.warning: Paused within one file, the Z zero of the first tool is kept: only if every tool has the same length.
help.postFirstToolChange.title: First tool change
help.postFirstToolChange.body: Sequence written at the first tool change of a file. The tool is already mounted and zeroed before the file runs: a pause there is useless.
help.postFirstToolChange.advice: Empty to keep the usual sequence; spindle stop and rise without pause for a Snapmaker.
export.simulationEmpty: Write the G-code at the previous step first: the simulation reads it back as the machine will.
